text.p: Atletico Madrid suffered a 4-1 mauling at home to Valencia in the Spanish first division on Saturday, a dismal prelude to next Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final against Ajax Amsterdam.
Atletico, who entertain Ajax in the second leg after a 1-1 draw in the first, have had a dreadful week, having been knocked out of the Spanish Cup by Barcelona last Wednesday.
Argentine international Ariel Ortega, who scored twice on his debut against Sevilla a week ago, had another outstanding game for Valencia and looks worth his tag as the club's most expensive signing.
Ortega, who moved to Valencia from Argentine club River Plate, pounced on the ball to score the opening goal after just eight minutes and then set up Xabier Eskurza for the second in the 26th minute.
Jose Ignacio Saenz made it 3-0 10 minutes before halftime when he found a gap in the defence and scored from inside the penalty area.
Jose Luis Caminero pulled one back for Atletico in the 51st minute but Valencia made it 4-1 in the final minute when Ortega passed for Brazil's Leandro Marchado to score.
Atletico hope for better fortune against Ajax. "On Wednesday we just can't make the same mistakes we made today," Atletico trainer Radomir Antic said.
In the day's other match, Deportivo Coruna joined second-placed Barcelona and Real Betis on 56 points, nine points behind leaders Real Madrid with a 1-0 win at Espanyol.
